primitives.name: Cox Process Event Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model - **Event processes (§3.1):** event types J = {home goals, away goals, home red cards, away red cards} each follow a Cox (doubly stochastic Poisson) process with intensity λ^j(t); conditional on λ^j, event times follow an inhomogeneous Poisson process.
primitives.latex: \lambda^j(t) \text{ is a stochastic intensity function dependent on observed events and time}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'λ^j(t)': 'event intensity per minute, dimensionless', 't': 'time in minutes, dimensionless'}
primitives.assumptions: Events occur according to a doubly stochastic Poisson process with time-varying intensity depending on match state.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When event occurrence exceeds model capacity or when regressors become stale post-substitution.

The core modeling approach leverages Cox processes to capture the stochastic nature of football events such as goals and red cards, treating them as doubly stochastic Poisson processes. Each event type has an intensity function λ^j(t) that evolves with match state. The log-linear structure ensures the likelihood is strictly concave, allowing for efficient convex optimization. Stoppage time is modeled separately as a Poisson variable dependent on halftime events. These primitives enable real-time forecasting of match outcomes and exact scores by conditioning on observed events and time. The model's strength lies in its ability to integrate temporal dependencies and external factors into a unified probabilistic framework. Failure modes include overfitting due to high-dimensional regressors, stale feature relevance post-substitution, and misalignment between discrete event times and continuous modeling assumptions.
